concepts.title: Empty Relation
concepts.definition: A relation on a set that holds no pair at all: the relation set is the empty collection, so nothing in the set relates to anything, itself included.
concepts.key_idea: The relation holds no ordered pair, so no element of the set relates to any element.
question_patterns: show that the relation a is sister of b on the set of students of a boys school is the empty relation
prove that R = {(a, b) : a - b = 10} on {1, 2, 3, 4} is the empty relation since no pair satisfies the condition
why is this relation called an empty relation justify
check whether R contains no ordered pairs at all
how many ordered pairs does the empty relation on set A contain

solution_steps.action: list the set and the pairing rule
solution_steps.explain: Write the set A and the condition that decides membership in R.

solution_steps.action: hunt for any pair that satisfies the rule
solution_steps.explain: Scan the ordered pairs of A x A for even one pair meeting the condition.
When no pair qualifies, R equals the empty set, so R is the empty relation.

concepts.title: Universal Relation
concepts.definition: A relation under which every ordered pair of the set with itself belongs to R, so each member relates to all members including itself; the relation equals the full Cartesian product.
concepts.key_idea: Every ordered pair of A x A lies in R, so all elements relate to all elements.
question_patterns: is the relation where heights differ by less than 3 meters on the set of students of a boys school a universal relation
show that the condition heights differ by less than 3 meters holds for every pair of students, so R = A x A is the universal relation
when do we call a relation universal on a set

verify that the relation equals the cartesian product A x A
state which relation on a set is called the universal relation

solution_steps.action: write the set and the rule
solution_steps.explain: State A and the condition defining R.

solution_steps.action: test an arbitrary pair from A x A
solution_steps.explain: Take any pair (a, b) of elements of A and apply the condition.

solution_steps.action: conclude R is the full product
solution_steps.explain: Since the condition holds for every pair, R coincides with A x A, the universal relation.

concepts.title: Reflexive Relation
concepts.definition: A relation on a set in which each member is paired with its own image: every element a of A must appear as the pair (a, a) inside R.
concepts.formula: (a, a) in R for every a in A
concepts.key_idea: Each element pairs with itself: the diagonal pairs (a, a) must all lie in R.
question_patterns: check whether the relation y is divisible by x on the set {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6} is reflexive
is the relation x is wife of y on a set of people reflexive justify
show that every element relates to itself under this relation
test the diagonal pairs (a, a) of the relation defined on integers
state the condition a relation must meet to be reflexive
determine whether R given by a <= b on the real numbers is reflexive

solution_steps.action: pick an arbitrary element a of A
solution_steps.explain: Let a range over every member of the set.

solution_steps.action: test the condition on the pair (a, a)
solution_steps.explain: Substitute a on both sides of the rule defining R.
If (a, a) lies in R for all a, R is reflexive; one failing element disproves it.

concepts.title: Symmetric Relation
concepts.definition: A relation that runs both ways: whenever the pair (a, b) belongs to R, the reversed pair (b, a) must belong to R as well.
concepts.formula: (a, b) in R implies (b, a) in R
concepts.key_idea: Reversed pairs must also belong: from (a, b) in R conclude (b, a) in R.
question_patterns: is the relation x is wife of y on a set of people symmetric justify
check whether x is exactly 7 cm taller than y gives a symmetric relation on a set of people

test whether the reverse of each pair also lies in R

determine whether the perpendicular relation on lines in a plane is symmetric

solution_steps.explain: Start from an arbitrary pair that satisfies the rule.
Use the same rule to check whether (b, a) must also satisfy it.
If the reverse always follows, R is symmetric; exhibit one unreversed pair to disprove.

concepts.title: Transitive Relation
concepts.definition: A relation where relatedness carries across a middle term: when a relates b and b relates c, the shortcut pair (a, c) must also sit in R.
concepts.formula: (a, b) in R and (b, c) in R implies (a, c) in R
concepts.key_idea: A chain of two pairs forces the third: (a, b) and (b, c) in R must give (a, c) in R.
question_patterns: is the relation x is father of y on a set of people transitive justify
check whether the relation y is divisible by x is transitive on {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}
show that a relates c whenever a relates b and b relates c

state what it means for a relation to be transitive
determine transitivity of the relation x is exactly 7 cm taller than y on people

solution_steps.explain: Assume (a, b) and (b, c) both belong to R.
Combine the two conditions through the rule defining R.
If every such chain closes with (a, c) in R, the relation is transitive; otherwise exhibit a broken chain.

concepts.title: Equivalence Relation
concepts.definition: A relation that is reflexive, symmetric and transitive at once; it behaves like equality inside the set by sorting elements into interchangeable groups.
concepts.formula: R reflexive and R symmetric and R transitive
concepts.key_idea: Reflexive plus symmetric plus transitive together give an equivalence relation, like divisibility by 2 on the set of integers.
question_patterns: show that the relation 2 divides a - b on the set of integers is an equivalence relation
prove that congruence of triangles is an equivalence relation on the set of all triangles in a plane
is x and y work at the same place an equivalence relation on a set of people justify
check all three properties reflexive symmetric transitive for the given relation
determine whether parallelism of lines in a plane is an equivalence relation
which three properties must a relation satisfy to be an equivalence relation

solution_steps.explain: Confirm (a, a) lies in R for every element a, so R is reflexive.
From (a, b) in R derive (b, a) in R, so R is symmetric.
From (a, b) and (b, c) in R derive (a, c) in R, so R is transitive.
With all three properties holding, R is an equivalence relation.

concepts.title: Equivalence Class and Partition
concepts.definition: For an equivalence relation, the class of an element is the bundle of all elements that relate to it; these pairwise disjoint bundles fill the whole set, forming its partition.
concepts.formula: [a] = set of all b in X with a R b
concepts.key_idea: Class [a] gathers all elements related to a; even and odd integers form the two classes of divisibility by 2, disjoint with union Z.
question_patterns: find the set of all elements related to 1 when the relation is |a - b| is a multiple of 4 on {0, 1, ..., 12}

Gather all b for which the pair (a, b) satisfies the relation.

solution_steps.action: report the class and the partition
solution_steps.explain: The collection [a] is the equivalence class; distinct classes are disjoint and their union is the whole set.

concepts.title: One-One (Injective) Function
concepts.definition: A function that never sends two different inputs to the same output: equal images force equal inputs, so distinct domain elements keep distinct images.
concepts.key_idea: Distinct inputs take distinct outputs, like roll numbers of students in a class: f(x1) = f(x2) must force x1 = x2.
question_patterns: show that the function assigning roll numbers to students of a class is one-one
check whether f(x) = 2x from N to N is one-one but not onto
determine whether f(x) = x^2 is injective on N, on Z and on R

prove that no two inputs of f produce the same output
state the test for a function to be one-one

solution_steps.explain: Assume f(x1) = f(x2) for inputs x1 and x2 of the domain.
Use algebra on the rule of f to see whether x1 must equal x2.
If equal images always force equal inputs, f is one-one; otherwise some output repeats and f is many-one.

concepts.title: Onto (Surjective) Function
concepts.definition: A function whose range exhausts the co-domain: each element of Y is hit by at least one input, leaving no outsider in Y.
concepts.key_idea: Range equals the co-domain: every y in Y is f of some x, which fails for f(x) = 2x from N to N since odd numbers are never hit.
question_patterns: is f(x) = 2x from N to N onto justify
check whether f(x) = x^2 from Z to Z is surjective
show that the greatest integer function f(x) = [x] is not onto R
determine whether every element of the co-domain has a pre-image
is the range of f equal to its co-domain justify
state the condition for a function to be onto

solution_steps.action: take an arbitrary co-domain value y
solution_steps.explain: Let y be any element of the co-domain Y.
Rearrange the rule of f to express a pre-image of y in the domain.
If the solved x is valid for every y, f is onto; a stranded co-domain value shows f is not onto.

concepts.title: Bijective Function
concepts.definition: A function that is both one-one and onto, pairing domain and co-domain elements perfectly one to one; only such maps can be inverted.
concepts.key_idea: One-one and onto together: distinct outputs for distinct inputs and every co-domain value hit, so f(x) = 2x on R is bijective.
question_patterns: show that f(x) = 2x from R to R is bijective
check injectivity and surjectivity of f(x) = 1/x on the non-zero real numbers
prove that f is both one-one and onto

determine whether the map pairs the two sets one-to-one and onto

solution_steps.explain: Show f(x1) = f(x2) forces x1 = x2.
Show every co-domain value y arises as f(x) for some domain element x.
With both properties verified, f is one-one and onto, hence bijective.

concepts.title: Composition of Functions
concepts.definition: Applying one function to the output of another: gof sends x through f first and then through g; order matters, and gof can differ from fog.
concepts.key_idea: Apply the inner function f first, then g: gof(x) = g(f(x)); for two linear rules the composite value at a point follows in two hops.
question_patterns: find gof(2) when f(x) = 2x + 3 and g(x) = 5x - 1 are linear functions

calculate the composite function value at the given point

solution_steps.explain: Run the inner function on x to get its image.
Feed the intermediate value into the outer function; the result is the composite value.

concepts.title: Invertible Function
concepts.definition: A function possessing a reverse map g with gof and fog both identity; for a linear rule, solving y = slope times x plus shift for x writes the inverse explicitly.
concepts.key_idea: Reverse a linear rule by subtracting the shift then dividing by the slope, exactly as in inverting f(x) = 4x + 3.
question_patterns: find the inverse of f(x) = 4x + 3 where Y collects values of the form 4x + 3

solution_steps.explain: Subtract the shift from the target output y.
Divide by the slope to isolate the pre-image; this value is the inverse evaluated at y.
